files_received.note: None of the listed src/data/research files were present in /home/workdir/attachments or elsewhere on this machine. Only the prior-round prompt markdown and the round-2 JSON this session already wrote were on disk. Source ids below are taken from Rule A in the prompt text, not from those files.

MU.basis: Primary, checkable source replacing the deep UN compendium page. Mauritius’s own SDDS DQAF metadata on the IMF DSBB, supplied by Statistics Mauritius, states that quarterly and annual national accounts follow SNA 2008. The same DSBB page points to Statistics Mauritius’s QNA methodology PDF.
MU.evidence_quote: The System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA2008) and the Quarterly National Accounts Manual, Concepts, Data Sources, and Compilation of the International Monetary Fund are followed as a general framework for compiling the Quarterly National Accounts statistics.

SL.basis: World Bank implementation-status document for the Harmonization of Core Social and Economic Statistics project names Statistics Sierra Leone’s 2024 adoption of 2008 SNA and the 2018 rebase. Consistent with earlier IMF STA TA (2022) that the rebase was designed to implement 2008 SNA.
SL.evidence_quote: Economic Statistics: Nearly all activities are complete. Major surveys and data sources have been finalised and published. The System of National Accounts 2008 was adopted in 2024, with GDP rebased to 2018. Ongoing work includes regular updates to the national accounts.

SL.basis: Statistics Sierra Leone’s own national-accounts/economic-statistics division page states that the CPI is compiled using COICOP. The Stats SL CPI Technical Methodological Guide has a dedicated COICOP chapter.
SL.evidence_quote: CPI is compiled using the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) for Household Final Consumption Expenditure with 2008 reference year.

IQ.basis: IMF 2020 Article IV informational annex is the last staff statement that names the SNA edition actually used. CSO national accounts mainly follow 1968 SNA. 2008 SNA appears only as a METAC TA objective, not as the current compilation standard — do not treat 2008 SNA as implemented.
IQ.evidence_quote: The national accounts mainly follow the 1968 System of National Accounts (SNA, 1968). The lack of regular, reliable and comprehensive source data for some industries and for GDP by expenditure undermine the quality of the national accounts. … Ongoing TA from METAC is helping the CSO to introduce a new base/benchmark year, to develop a set of supply and use tables, and to improve the compilation methodology and coverage of GDP based on the 2008 SNA guidelines.

IQ.basis: Same 2020 Article IV informational annex, plus Iraq’s own e-GDDS BOP metadata on the DSBB (updated 8 January 2018): CBI reports BOP in BPM6 format and classifies transactions largely in accordance with BPM6.
IQ.evidence_quote: The CBI compiles and reports annual as well as quarterly balance of payments data in the format of the IMF’s Balance of Payments Manual, sixth edition (BPM6) to the IMF.

IQ.basis: Restated on a primary IMF staff annex (not ODIN). Participation since 2009; no NSDP. Already minted; included only as the 2020 annex restatement if you want a second cite on the existing edge.
IQ.evidence_quote: Iraq has been participating in e-GDDS since 2009 but has not yet launched a National Summary Data Page for the dissemination of key macroeconomic statistics.

SD.basis: Most recent IMF Article IV that names an SNA edition (2020). Staff report states national accounts are still on 1968 SNA with base year 1981; latest official NA data then were from 2016. A 2025 IMF TA note discusses a future review of alignment with SNA 2008 — that is not yet an implemented methodology, so no sna-2008 edge.
SD.evidence_quote: National accounts are based on 1968 SNA with a base year of 1981 and have weaknesses in quality and timeliness—the latest data are from 2016.

SD.basis: COMESA’s official statistics mandate (Treaty Article 140) plus the UN Handbook of Statistical Organization country card listing Sudan among COMESA member states whose statistics the COMESA Statistics Unit is charged with collecting and harmonising.
SD.evidence_quote: Member States: Burundi, Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Djibouti, Egypt, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Eswatini, Kenya, Libya, Malawi, Madagascar, Mauritius, Rwanda, Seychelles, Somalia, Sudan, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe. … Statistical Development and management in COMESA is guided by Article 140 of the Treaty. The Treaty provisions state that Member States undertake to co-operate in the field of statistics in order to create an enabling environment for the regular flow of up-to-date, reliable, harmonised and comparable statistical data

IR.basis: Iran’s own e-GDDS national-accounts metadata on the IMF DSBB, as provided by the authorities. CBI compiles the accounts; the named frameworks are SNA 1968 and SNA 1993, not 2008 SNA. No later official SCI/CBI page opened for this round states a completed 2008 SNA changeover.
IR.evidence_quote: The Central Bank of Iran (CBI) compiles and publishes Iran’s national accounts statistics. These national accounts are based on the United Nations, System of National Accounts (SNA 1968 and 1993).

AF.basis: Afghanistan’s own GDDS national-accounts metadata on the DSBB, last updated 1 June 2006 — the same month metadata were first posted. Names SNA 1993 as the framework then in use, and dates the 2002–2004 switch from the Material Product System.
AF.evidence_quote: Currently, the national accounts estimates broadly follow the concepts, definitions, and classifications of the System of National Accounts 1993 (SNA 1993), as the basic data availability permit. … For the period 2002-2004 the National Accounts Division compiled the estimates based on SNA 1993.

AF.basis: Corroboration of the June 2006 GDDS entry, without relying on the hard-to-retrieve CR 06/251 Executive Director statement. The DSBB country NA page is itself dated 1 June 2006 and is the metadata that the important-dates table records as first posted 22 June 2006.
AF.evidence_quote: Afghanistan, Islamic Republic of. National Accounts (GDP). Last Updated: Jun 01, 2006.

YE.basis: Not a current compilation claim. IMF 2025 Article IV and the World Bank MPISY project document both state that official national accounts have not been compiled by CSO-Aden or Sana’a since 2014. The World Bank project names SNA 2008 only as a planned training/compilation target. Kept as cites (context), not methodology_depends_on.
YE.evidence_quote: Yemen’s system of national accounts (SNA) has effectively collapsed: no official national accounts have been compiled by CSO-Aden or Sana’a since 2014; data collection from enterprises is absent; regular statistical business processes (administrative records, collection, processing, quality control, dissemination) are not in place

SY.basis: Syria’s own e-GDDS CPI metadata on the IMF DSBB (last updated 23 February 2011). Classification ‘largely follows’ COICOP. Dated; CBS was later merged (2025) into the Planning and Statistics Commission, so treat as a last-stated official methodology, not proof of a living 2026 CPI series.
SY.evidence_quote: The CPI items are classified according to a national classification that largely follows the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP).

MU.june_2016_changeover_on_statsmauritius_o: Statistics Mauritius’s current DSBB DQAF and live ESI/QNA releases state that SNA 2008 is the framework now used. They do not, on the pages opened this round, repeat the June 2016 changeover sentence that appeared only in the UN National Accounts compendium. The 2016 date is therefore not re-asserted from a Stats Mauritius PDF.

SD.sna-2008: 2025 IMF TA (tarea2025110) says a later phase will evaluate alignment with SNA 2008 and prepare for SNA 2025. That is planned work, not current compilation. No CBS methodology page opened this round claims 2008 SNA.
SD.imf-bpm6: No Central Bank of Sudan or CBS quote opened this round that names BPM6 (or BPM5) as the BOP manual in force.
SD.un-coicop: No CBS CPI methodology page opened this round that names a COICOP edition.
SD.aitrs: AITRS describes itself as serving all Arab statistical offices / 22 Arab states. No AITRS roster, minutes, or accession record opened this round names Sudan’s CBS specifically. Null rather than infer from League membership.

SL.imf-bpm6: Stats SL NSDS text assigns BPM adoption to the Bank of Sierra Leone, which is not in the Rule A source list. No sl-statssl page opened this round claims Stats SL compiles BOP on BPM6.
SL.ecowas-stats: ECOWAS Regional Economic Outlook 2023 names Sierra Leone as a member and prints SL growth/inflation figures, but that is an ECOWAS analytical publication using national data, not a Stats SL statement that it compiles to an ECOWAS statistical standard. Not minted as methodology_depends_on.

IQ.sna-2008: Named only as the destination of METAC TA, not as the edition CSO currently compiles on.
IQ.un-coicop: No CSO CPI methodology note opened this round that names a COICOP edition.
IQ.aitrs: Same as Sudan: no country-named AITRS primary document opened.

IR.sna-2008: DSBB metadata names SNA 1968 and 1993. No official SCI or CBI page opened this round states completed adoption of 2008 SNA.
IR.imf-bpm6: CBI publishes a Balance of Payments page and tables but the pages opened do not name BPM6 or BPM5. Null.
IR.un-coicop: No SCI CPI methodology page opened that names COICOP.
IR.aitrs: Iran is not an Arab League state; AITRS current membership is Arab NSOs. Historical 1971 Near-East institute membership is pre-1977 and not used.

AF.sna-2008: No NSIA/CSO or post-2006 IMF annex opened this round that states Afghanistan compiles on 2008 SNA. WEO 2015 Table G still listed Afghanistan as SNA 1993 / BPM 5.
AF.imf-bpm6: WEO 2015 Table G listed Afghanistan BOP source manual as BPM 5. No later official DAB/NSIA quote naming BPM6 was opened.
AF.un-coicop: No NSIA CPI methodology page opened that names COICOP.
AF.cr_06_251_ed_statement: The round-2 quote from IMF Country Report 06/251 about STA indicating imminent GDDS participation remains unre-verified from a page-numbered public extract in this round. Substituted the 1 June 2006 DSBB NA metadata page, which is retrievable and contemporaneous with the 22 June 2006 posting date.

YE.current_sna_edition: No official national accounts have been compiled by CSO-Aden or Sana’a since 2014 (World Bank MPISY PAD; IMF 2025 AIV). Cannot attach methodology_depends_on to sna-2008 or sna-1993 as a living compilation rule.
YE.imf-bpm6: IMF 2025 AIV describes STA-supported external-sector estimates and a planned ESS mission; it does not quote CSO or CBY saying they compile a BPM6 BOP.
YE.un-coicop: No CSO CPI methodology note opened that names a COICOP edition.
YE.gcc-stat: Yemen is not a GCC member. No GCC-Stat roster naming Yemen was opened.
YE.aitrs: No country-named AITRS primary document opened.

SY.sna-any: No CBS national-accounts methodology page or post-2009 Article IV statistical annex was opened that names an SNA edition. Last completed Article IV was 26 February 2010. Null.
SY.imf-bpm6: No CBS or Central Bank of Syria BOP methodology quote naming BPM6/BPM5 was opened.
SY.aitrs: No country-named AITRS primary document opened.

proposed_reports.title: National Accounts Estimates (Economic and Social Indicators)
proposed_reports.description: Recurring official GDP/GVA release. Latest issue opened: Economic and Social Indicators Issue No 1937, National Accounts Estimates, June 2026 issue, covering 2023–2026, released 30 June 2026. Statistics Mauritius also issues a separate Quarterly National Accounts ESI (e.g. Issue No 1902, 3rd Quarter 2025) and historically an annual Digest of National Accounts. This is the missing domestic NA node the sna-2008 edge should attach to once minted; until then the edge is parked on mu-statsmauritius.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: National Accounts Estimates ESI: quarterly (March, June, September, December). Quarterly National Accounts ESI: quarterly. Digest of National Accounts: annual (historical series).

proposed_reports.title: System of National Accounts 1968
proposed_reports.publisher: United Nations Statistical Commission / United Nations
proposed_reports.description: Predecessor SNA edition. Still the named compilation framework for Sudan (IMF 2020 Article IV) and, mainly, Iraq (IMF 2020 Article IV informational annex).
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: Standing methodological standard (superseded as the recommended edition by SNA 1993 then SNA 2008).

proposed_reports.title: System of National Accounts 1993
proposed_reports.publisher: United Nations, IMF, World Bank, OECD, Eurostat
proposed_reports.description: Named compilation framework on the DSBB for Afghanistan (2006 metadata) and, jointly with SNA 1968, for Iran’s CBI national accounts.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: Standing methodological standard (superseded as the recommended edition by SNA 2008).

proposed_reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Sixth Edition (BPM6)
proposed_reports.description: IMF external-sector compilation standard. Named by the IMF 2020 Article IV informational annex as the format in which the Central Bank of Iraq compiles and reports BOP.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: Standing manual (2009); BPM7 released 2025 with a 2029–2030 implementation window.

proposed_reports.title: Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP)
proposed_reports.description: International classification for household consumption / CPI baskets. Named by Statistics Sierra Leone for its CPI and by Syria’s DSBB CPI metadata.

proposed_reports.title: COMESA statistical cooperation (Treaty Article 140 / COMESA Committee on Statistical Matters / COMESA Statistics Unit)
proposed_reports.publisher: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa
proposed_reports.description: Regional statistical body whose member-state roster includes Sudan (and Mauritius). Treaty Article 140 commits members to cooperate on harmonised statistics.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: Standing treaty obligation; COMSTAT databases and COMESA statistical publications updated on a programme cycle.
